rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one grasps the Event's true nature or full severity; worldly calamities and fire are negligible beside it, and the surah's closing description of blazing fire echoes its opening warning.
rows.anchor: لأنها في الشدة بحيث لا يبلغها وهم أحد ولا فهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording differs because the striking Event is perceptible, whereas the Abyss is not; therefore the verse asks what the Event is but not what the Abyss is.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its details can be known only through God's report, since they concern events that will occur rather than necessary duties and have no proof except transmitted revelation.
rows.anchor: لأنه بحث عن وقوع الوقعات لا عن وجوب الواجبات

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The verifiers say the repeated warning about the Striking Event is rhetorically stronger than the repeated warning about the Inevitable, since the later expression must intensify the alert.
rows.anchor: ثم قال المحققون قوله : { القارعة ما القارعة } أشد من قوله : { الحاقة ما الحاقة } لأن النازل آخرا لابد وأن يكون أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In meaning, the Inevitable is stronger because it conveys justice, while the Striking Event is stronger in its assault on hearts with a terrifying occurrence.
rows.anchor: فالحاقة أشد لكونه راجعا إلى معنى العدل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the pronoun as referring to the calamity implied by the preceding statement that the person's mother is an abyss.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : ( هيه ) ضمير الداهية التي دل عليها قوله : { فأمه هاوية }

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-Zamakhshari takes the pronoun to refer directly to the Abyss itself.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : ( هيه ) ضمير الداهية التي دل عليها قوله : { فأمه هاوية } في التفسير ( الثالث ) : أو ضمير ( هاوية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final hāʾ is a pause letter that may be omitted in connected recitation; stopping with it is preferred to follow the muṣḥaf, where it is written, as in the other cited forms.
rows.anchor: والهاء للسكت فإذا وصل جاز حذفها والاختيار الوقف بالهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benefactions include averting harm and bringing benefit; averting harm is prior, so the previous surah recounts protection while this one recounts provision and security.
rows.anchor: فلهذا السبب بين تعالى نعمة دفع الضرر في سورة الفيل ونعمة جلب النفع في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say self-protection from harm is obligatory, whereas the acquisition of benefit is not obligatory.
rows.anchor: قالوا : دفع الضرر عن النفس واجب أما جلب النفع [ فإنه ] غير واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because blessing calls for gratitude and worship, God follows the mention of the favor with a demand for worship.
rows.anchor: لا جرم أتبع ذكر النعمة بطلب العبودية فقال : { فليعبدوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship means humbling oneself and submitting to the worshiped one to the utmost degree.
rows.anchor: العبادة هي التذلل والخضوع للمعبود على غاية ما يكون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the command as calling the Quraysh to affirm God's oneness: He alone protected the House, not the idols, and monotheism is the key to worship.
rows.anchor: ثم قال بعضهم : أراد فليوحدوا رب هذا البيت

rows.speaker: منهم
rows.claim: Others take the command to mean the acts of worship performed by the limbs, including each category of such worship.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : المراد العبادات المتعلقة بأعمال الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the comprehensive interpretation, since the wording covers every kind of worship unless evidence excludes one.
rows.anchor: والأولى حمله على الكل لأن اللفظ متناول للكل إلا ما أخرجه الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation tells the Quraysh to abandon their winter and summer journeys and devote themselves to worship, because God feeds them and makes them secure.
rows.anchor: فليتركوا رحلة الشتاء والصيف وليشتغلوا بعبادة رب هذا البيت فإنه يطعمهم من جوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the House's Lord recalls the Quraysh's claim to Abraha that the House had a Lord who would protect it; having relied on Him rather than idols, they must direct worship and service to Him.
rows.anchor: تخصيص لفظ الرب تقرير لما قالوه لأبرهة : إن للبيت ربا سيحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to the House magnifies it through reciprocal associations: God calls people His servants, people call Him their God, God names Himself the House's Lord, and the House is His own.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى البيت في هذا النظم تفيد التعظيم فإنه سبحانه تارة أضاف العبد إلى نفسه فيقول : { يا عبادي } وتارة يضيف نفسه إلى العبد فيقول : { وإلهكم } كذا في البيت [ تارة ] يضيف نفسه إلى البيت وهو قوله : { فليعبدوا رب هذا البيت } وتارة يضيف البيت إلى نفسه فيقول : { طهرا بيتي }
